Attachment.description:
Something the user attached to their message — a pasted screenshot, a
dragged-in file, an editor selection.

The variants below are the three shapes hosts actually have, so that a host
can hand over whichever it already holds instead of being forced to pre-read
(or pre-decode) on the runtime's behalf.

anything else is inlined as text.
Use this when the host only has a path — e.g. a drag-and-drop.

Text the host has already read. `path` is kept for the label shown to
the model, and may be a synthetic name for non-file text such as an
editor selection.

An image the host already decoded — the clipboard-paste case, where
there is no file on disk at all. `data` is base64 without a data-URI
prefix.

A PDF the host already encoded. `data` is base64 without a data-URI
prefix; `name` is the label the model and the provider see.

PermissionDecision.description:
Wire shape: `{"type":"permit"}` / `{"type":"deny","reason":"..."}` /
`{"type":"permit_always","scope":"session"}` /
`{"type":"permit_always","scope":"local"}` — what
`session.respondToPrompt` (daemon RPC) parses out of its `decision`
param and what `InputMessage::PermissionResponse` carries.

oneOf.description:
Like `Permit`, but also persists an Allow rule beyond this single
tool call — see `base::interface::permission::PermissionGrants`.
`scope: Session` keeps it in-memory only (rest of this session);
`scope: Local` additionally writes it to `.agix/settings.local.json`
so future sessions in this project inherit it too.
Prompt user for each tool call that isn't explicitly allowed.

Allow file writes inside the project (the working directory and
`sandbox.additional_directories`) and read-only calls without asking;
ask about the rest, as `default` does. Writes into the project's
`.git`, `.agix`, `.claude` and `.agents/skills` still ask.

Ask nothing and skip the rules of the user's tiers. Credentials
(`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, the state directory's settings and tokens)
are still refused, the deployment's managed `deny` / `ask` rules still
apply, input that is not valid is still refused, and `Bash` still runs
in the OS sandbox. `auto` and `yolo` are accepted as other spellings
of this mode and read back as `bypassPermissions`.
Plan mode — only allow read-only tools.
Don't ask — deny any tool not explicitly allowed (no prompt).

left to `session.rename`. `None` or `true`: as its scene says.

clock.description:
Where this session's kept time starts (the date in its prompt, its log's timestamps).
Omitted: the machine's clock — except in replay, where it starts when the recording did.

host_tools.description:
Tools this session's host runs itself, offered to the model as the
session's own; a call to one is a `host_tool_call` frame, answered
with `session.respondToolCall`.

model.description:
The conversation's model. `None` takes the provider's `default_model`
when `provider` is given, the settings' model otherwise.

output_schema.description:
JSON Schema the session's structured output must satisfy — see
`runtime::agent::Builder::output_schema`.

permission_mode.description:
This session's permission mode. `None` takes the settings'
`permission_mode`. A session may always ask for a stricter mode than
the settings'; a looser one is clamped unless the settings set
`allow_client_permission_override`.

permission_rules.description:
Allow/deny/ask rules for the `Policy` this session's
`permission_mode` (if set) constructs. Ignored when `permission_mode`
is `None`.

prompt.description:
A system-prompt append / override for this session's own agent, over
the settings files'. Its delegates do not get it.

prompt_types.description:
The kinds of `prompt` frame this session's host answers: `permission`
always, `question` and `mcp_elicitation` when listed. Names this daemon does not know are
ignored rather than voiding the options.

provider.description:
The provider this session's conversation goes to, by its id in
`providers`. `None` follows the settings' routing. Sub-agents,
compaction and the other routed tasks keep the settings' routing
either way.

skill_dirs.description:
Skill directories of the host's for this session, merged over the
tiers by name: a built-in, a package's or an untrusted project's skill
yields to one of these; the user's tiers and a trusted project's do
not. Of two listed directories the first wins a name. Read-only to
every session.

SessionPrompt.description:
What [`Builder::session_prompt`] puts over a session's settings. `None`
leaves the settings' `prompt_append` / `prompt_override` in force.

SessionRef.description: Params that name one session and nothing else.

generation.description: Which engine the session is on; each rebuild brings up the next.

active.description:
Whether the engine is in memory; when it is not, only scheduled jobs
are listed.

SetGoalParams.description: Params that name one session and nothing else.

hooks.description:
Each entry a `HostHookOption`; `[]` or `null` withdraws them all.
Read one by one: a bad entry is refused alone.

host_tools.description:
Each entry as `options.host_tools` takes it; `[]` withdraws them all.
Read one by one: a bad entry is refused alone.

append.description:
A string sets it, `null` clears it back to the settings files', an
absent key leaves it.

skill_dirs.description: The whole set, replacing the one before; `[]` clears it.

SkillConflict.description: A package skill whose name another source holds.

path.description: Absolute, on the machine the engine runs on. Need not exist yet.

SkillDirReport.description: What one of the host's skill directories gives a session.

shadowed.description: Its skills another source holds in the session.

skills.description: The skills this directory has the name of in the session, sorted.

oneOf.description: Not there; read once it is.

Recorded, but left out when the session was brought back: it no
longer passes the checks `options.skill_dirs` is held to.

provider.description: Refused when given: a sub-agent runs on its parent's provider.

StopReason.description: 模型停止原因。Anthropic API 取值。

oneOf.description:
+**: agent hit `EngineConfig.max_api_calls_per_turn`. Not from
the Anthropic API — emitted by our engine when the configured per-
turn budget is exhausted. Caller (e.g. `AgentTool` for sub-agents)
should handle gracefully: return whatever partial work exists,
flagged but **not** is_error=true. Carries the same
`max_turns_reached` attachment + early-return semantics.
兜底未来新增：避免反序列化失败

stopped.description: `false`: no such task, or it had already ended.

resume.description: Resume the session first when it is not in memory.

last_seq.description: The transcript watermark to catch up to (protocol §5.6).

chars.description: `None` when the recording no longer holds the block.

cache.description: `ephemeral` / `global` cache marking, when the block had one.

TaskInfo.description: A task as `session.tasks` lists it and the `task_*` events carry it.

waiting_for.description: The prompt ids the work waits on; empty unless `status` is `waiting`.

TaskModelOverride.description:
A `task_models.<task>` entry. Accepts either the shorthand `"provider_id"`
string form or the detailed `{ "provider": ..., "model": ... }` object form.

TaskOutput.description:
Part of what one task has produced. Offsets count every byte the work
ever printed.

final.description: The output has ended; `next_byte` will not grow.

TaskOutputParams.description: One of `tail_bytes` and `from_byte`; neither: the last 8 KiB.

oneOf.description: Alive with nothing to do: a persistent team member between messages.
Running, and waiting on the host to answer a question.

ToolResultContent.description:
`tool_result.content` 字段：string 或 ContentBlock 数组。

`#[serde(untagged)]` 让 JSON `"hello"` 直接解到 Text 变体，`[…]` 解到 Blocks。

input.description: The arguments; for a call whose arguments did not parse, the raw text.

TrustLevel.description: What a project no `trusted` pattern names is.

TrustSource.description: What decided that a project is trusted or not.

oneOf.description: `project_trust.default`: nobody has said anything about this project.
A `trusted` pattern in the global `settings.json`.

A `trusted` pattern in the global `settings.local.json`, where
`project.trust` records the host's answer.
No project tier of its own.

name.description: The session's name after the turn.

TurnReply.description:
How a turn went, as `session.run_turn`, `session.compact` and
`session.clear` answer it.

TurnState.description: What a session in memory is doing; a session not in memory is idle.

oneOf.description: Being rebuilt in place on its next engine.

Held by an operation other than a turn — a look at or a change to
its context.

UpdateGoalParams.description: Params that name one session and nothing else.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description:
Tokens written into the prompt cache by this call, and tokens read
back from it. Both are priced differently from ordinary input — a
cache read costs a fraction of one — so a report that folded them
into `input_tokens` would overcharge and one that dropped them
undercharges by whatever the cache covered.

`#[serde(default)]` because recordings written before these existed
must still read back.

VisibleText.description: A piece of text that will reach the model, and where it came from.
